candidate.claim: Order-swap inconsistency is a directly tested label-free trigger for selectively escalating pairwise LLM evaluator computation; it concentrates updates on cases with larger measured benefit, while missing consistent-but-wrong cases and becoming expensive when the base judge is broadly unstable.

primary_source.title: Becoming Experienced Judges: Selective Test-Time Learning for Evaluators

selection_signal.definition: The vanilla judge evaluates both A-vs-B and B-vs-A. A response-order-dependent verdict is self-inconsistent and triggers Selective LWE meta-prompt updating; stable verdicts skip the expensive update path.
selection_signal.base_cost: The Selective LWE budget includes two vanilla passes used for the consistency check.

gpt_4_1_main_table.metrics: Pair Accuracy requires both original and swapped predictions to be correct; Relative Inference Cost is total input+output character length normalized to vanilla.
gpt_4_1_main_table.cost_ratio_selective_to_full: 3.9/10.9 ~= 35.8%; the paper describes this as approximately 36% of LWE
gpt_4_1_main_table.selective_cost_decomposition: two vanilla passes for consistency checking plus an additional 1.9x for LWE on flagged cases
gpt_4_1_main_table.ordering_repeats: LWE and Selective LWE main results are averaged over three random test-case orderings.

inconsistent_subset.interpretation: The intervention is substantially more helpful on the cases selected by order-swap inconsistency in this setup.

consistent_subset_and_blind_spot.clarification: Table 4 applies full LWE as an ablation to consistent examples; it is not Selective LWE, which by design skips updates there. The MM result shows that updating consistent cases can reduce accuracy.

backbone_generalization_and_cost_failure.cause_reported_by_paper: Claude produces inconsistent judgments on over 50% of the test sets, so Selective LWE intervenes much more frequently and its cost rises sharply.

batching.finding: Updating every sample (b=1) is most expensive and not necessarily best; b=8 degrades as update context becomes long/unstable; b=4 is the selected balance in the tested inconsistent subsets.
batching.scope: The HTML text describes this non-monotonic result but this audit did not digitize every point in Figure 7.

weak_model_failure.detail: The limitations section reports that Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct often fails to produce valid evaluation prompts after meta-prompt updates, so the method depends on base evaluator capability.

scope_clarifications: The direct experiment is sequential evaluator meta-prompt adaptation on two pairwise multimodal reward benchmarks, not evolutionary archive replacement or MAP-Elites. Transfer from selective judging to search-controller survival decisions is a hypothesis.

Order-swap inconsistency is a useful selection signal, not a correctness certificate. The source explicitly exposes hundreds of stable-but-wrong cases, so a controller that never audits stable decisions can systematically miss errors.
The 3.9x and 10.9x costs are normalized input/output CHARACTER LENGTH, not measured wall-clock, API dollars or exact tokenizer counts. Avoid calling 3.9x a token-cost ratio without qualification.
Selective LWE itself includes a two-pass order-swap probe, so 'selective' does not mean near-zero overhead on stable cases.

High instability can destroy the cost advantage: Claude Sonnet 4.5 reaches 15.2x because more than half of cases trigger updates. Therefore selective escalation needs a fallback/cap when the trigger rate is high.

The inconsistent-subset 125/248->189/248 and 62/137->92/137 comparisons are from run 0, whereas the headline main table averages three random-order runs. Do not mix their uncertainty/repetition scopes.

The consistent-subset comparison is Vanilla vs full LWE, not Vanilla vs Selective LWE. It supports the idea that uniform updating can be low-value or harmful on stable cases, but does not measure what Selective LWE would do there because it skips those updates.
confidence: high for primary tables, subset counts and limitations; medium for transfer to population/QD search
unresolved: Matched-budget archive/search experiment where order-swap inconsistency directly controls re-judging or survival/archive replacement and final search quality is measured.
Stable-wrong sentinel audit policy comparing random audits versus other perturbation/uncertainty probes at equal cost.
A trigger-rate cap/fallback policy for regimes where most judgments are unstable, preserving useful verification without 15x+ overhead.
downstream_instruction: Retain C28 as direct evidence that a cheap decision-invariance probe can concentrate evaluator adaptation on cases with larger measured benefit, while explicitly carrying the stable-wrong blind spot, two-pass probe cost, character-length cost metric, and high-trigger-rate cost failure. Do not claim it directly improves evolutionary archive quality.
